questions.question: Describe why independence is considered a fundamental principle for constitutional bodies.
questions.solution_html:
• Independence ensures impartiality of constitutional bodies —protects them from political
  • interference—upholds credibility in governance.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: List the powers of the National Commission for Minorities.
questions.solution_html:
• NCM investigates minority rights issues —advises government on policies —monitors
  • safeguards for minorities.

questions.question: Explain the background and reasons for the establishment of NITI Aayog.

  • federalism and policy innovation.

questions.question: Assess the effectiveness of constitutional bodies in maintaining checks and balances in the Indian political system.
questions.solution_html:
• Constitutional bodies check executive power —ensure accountability —strengthen
  • democratic balance though challenges remain.

questions.question: Examine the limitations of the CAG in the Indian administrative system.
questions.solution_html:
• CAG cannot enforce recommendations —limited to auditing —depends on legislature for
  • action- reducing impact.

questions.question: Explain the constitutional position of the Attorney General of India under Article 76.
questions.solution_html:
• Attorney General is chief legal advisor—appointed by President—enjoys right of audience
  • in courts under Article 76.

questions.question: Discuss the mechanisms to ensure accountabilty and transperancey of Constitutional and Statutory Bodies in India?
questions.solution_html:
• Accountability of bodies ensured through parliamentary oversight—transparency promoted
  • by audits, reports and RTI—judicial review strengthens credibility and public trust.

questions.question: Discuss the constitutional foundation and institutional importance of the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
questions.solution_html:
• NCST established under Article 338A —safeguards rights of Scheduled Tribes —advises
  • government on policies and monitors implementation of constitutional protections.

questions.question: Describe the structure and composition of the National Green Tribunal.

  • judicial—changing role reflects governance needs and citizen-centric accountability.
